user.title: Evac Relay setup (1 of 6): welcome
user.description:
Evac Relay turns county evacuation alerts into house-wide alarms: speakers, TVs, phones, and a scanner stream.

**It is not an official alert system.** It relays alerts you already receive, can be delayed or fail (power, internet, email), and never replaces Wireless Emergency Alerts, county texts and calls, or following official instructions. Keep those turned on.

Confirm the home location below. It is used for National Weather Service alerts.

data.name: Name for this home
data.acknowledge_disclaimer: I understand this supplements, and does not replace, official alerts

zones.title: Step 2 of 6: your evacuation zones
zones.description:
1. Open the [Genasys Protect map]({zone_url}) and search your address.
2. Copy the zone ID shown on the zone card, exactly as written.
3. Add any other zones you care about (a parent's house, school, work), one per line.

Alerts that name one of these zones sound the alarm. Alerts for other zones only notify you. Leave this empty to treat every evacuation message sent to you as yours; {alert_system} already targets messages by the addresses you register.

county_alerts.title: Step 3 of 6: sign up for {alert_system}
county_alerts.description:
Evac Relay listens to the same alerts your county sends to people.

1. Enroll at [{alert_system}]({alert_signup_url}).
2. Register your home address (and any other addresses matching the zones you entered).
3. Add an **email address that Home Assistant will read** as one of your email contacts. A dedicated Gmail account works best.
4. Keep text and voice alerts going to your own phones too.

You can finish this later; Home Assistant will remind you under Settings > Repairs.

data.county_alerts_registered: I've enrolled and added the email Home Assistant will read

email.title: Step 4 of 6: connect the alert email
email.description:
Home Assistant reads alert email with its built-in IMAP integration. IMAP accounts found: **{imap_status}**.

If you haven't added one yet:
1. For Gmail, turn on 2-step verification and [create an app password]({gmail_app_password_url}).
2. In Gmail, make a filter that labels mail from {alert_system} (for example label `evac`).
3. Add the [IMAP integration]({imap_docs_url}) with server `imap.gmail.com`, port 993, folder = that label, search `UNSEEN`.
4. Come back through Settings > Devices & services > Evac Relay > Configure to select it.

You can skip this now and connect it later.

scanner.title: Step 5 of 6: scanner radio
scanner.description:
During an alarm Evac Relay can play a live fire/EMS scanner feed on your speakers.

1. Find a {county} fire feed in the [Broadcastify directory]({scanner_directory_url}).
2. Paste the feed's direct stream URL here. Some feeds and ad-free streams need a Broadcastify Premium account.

Optional. Test it by playing the URL on one speaker before relying on it.

nws.title: Step 6 of 6: National Weather Service
nws.description: NWS alerts are a free backup source. They don't include county evacuation zones, so by default they notify you without sounding the full alarm.

data.nws_enabled: Watch NWS alerts for this location
data.nws_triggers_alarm: Let NWS evacuation-type alerts sound the full alarm

finish.title: Almost done
finish.description: Finish now, or add a Twilio phone number so county texts and robocalls reach Home Assistant directly.

twilio.title: Advanced: Twilio number
twilio.description:
1. Buy a local number in Twilio and upgrade the account (trial accounts can't receive short codes).
2. Ask Twilio support to enable receiving SMS from short codes. Delivery is still not guaranteed, so voice matters.
3. Register the Twilio number in your county alerts as both a **text** and a **voice** contact.
4. Paste your Twilio auth token here. After setup, Home Assistant shows the webhook URLs to paste into Twilio. With Home Assistant Cloud (Nabu Casa) the URL is created automatically.

data.twilio_allowed_from: Only accept from these numbers (optional, comma separated)

data_description.public_webhook_url: Leave empty to use Nabu Casa or your external URL. Set only if Twilio reaches Home Assistant through something else, such as Cloudflare. It must match exactly what Twilio calls.

error.disclaimer_required: Please confirm you understand this is not an official alert system.
error.invalid_zones: Enter zone IDs exactly as the county writes them, such as LAK-E123, separated by commas or new lines. Place names and entries like Zone 5 are too generic to match safely.
error.invalid_url: Enter a full URL starting with http:// or https://
error.page_not_stream: That is the feed's web page, not the audio stream. Speakers need the direct stream URL. Broadcastify now serves direct streams only to Premium accounts, as https://USERNAME:PASSWORD@audio.broadcastify.com/FEEDID.mp3; that URL contains your password, so Evac Relay keeps it out of history.
error.https_required: The public webhook URL must start with https://
error.twilio_token_required: A Twilio auth token is required so every request can be verified.
error.no_sources: Turn on at least one alert source: email, NWS, or Twilio.

no_email_source.title: Evac Relay is not reading county alert email
no_email_source.description: Evac Relay for {name} has no email account selected, so county evacuation email will not sound the alarm. Add the IMAP integration for the address registered with your county alerts, then select it under Evac Relay > Configure > Zones and alert sources.

county_not_registered.title: Finish county alert sign-up
county_not_registered.description: Evac Relay for {name} is set up, but you haven't confirmed enrolling in {alert_system} with the email Home Assistant reads. Enroll at {alert_signup_url}, then check the box under Evac Relay > Configure > Zones and alert sources.

imap_entry_missing.title: Evac Relay is watching an email account that no longer exists
imap_entry_missing.description: Evac Relay for {name} has an email account selected that was removed or re-added. County evacuation email from it will not sound the alarm. Open Evac Relay > Configure > Zones and alert sources and select the current IMAP account.

twilio_url_unavailable.title: Evac Relay has no public Twilio webhook URL
twilio_url_unavailable.description: Evac Relay for {name} could not get a public URL for Twilio. Texts and calls to your Twilio number will not reach Home Assistant. If you use Home Assistant Cloud, this usually fixes itself once the cloud connects. Otherwise set an external URL in Home Assistant, or a public webhook URL override in Evac Relay > Configure > Twilio.

twilio_signature.title: Twilio requests are being rejected
twilio_signature.description: Evac Relay for {name} rejected several Twilio requests because their signature didn't match. Check that the webhook URLs in Twilio exactly match the ones Evac Relay showed, and that the auth token is current.

blueprint_outdated.title: The Evac Relay alarm blueprint has an update
blueprint_outdated.description: The blueprint file at {path} differs from the version bundled with this Evac Relay release and was not written by Evac Relay, so it is treated as your own edit and left alone. To take the new version, rename or delete that file and reload Evac Relay; it will be reinstalled, and existing automations keep their settings.

twilio_error.title: Evac Relay could not process a Twilio request
twilio_error.description: Evac Relay for {name} hit an error handling a text or call from Twilio. Check the Home Assistant log for details and report it on the Evac Relay issue tracker. Email and NWS alerts are not affected.
